candidates.recommended_angle: Straightforward consumer-safety explainer: what's contaminated, which brands/lots, health risk level, and disposal/refund guidance — framed as a quick-reference utility piece, not alarmist.
candidates.why_now: FDA-issued recall reported 9/29 by EatingWell; not yet covered in our recent recall coverage (chlorthalidone, thyroid meds, meat, jalapeño products).
candidates.primary_headline: FDA Recalls Sugar Over Contamination — What to Know Before You Bake
candidates.next_steps: Hold for FDA.gov confirmation before publishing; recheck for 2-3 more outlet pickups to raise confidence to High.
integrity_flags: Single media source identified (EatingWell) as of this run — confirm against FDA.gov recall notice number/lot codes before publishing.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Breaking recall with FDA backing but single-source news pickup limits trend signal.
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: High consumer search intent (product identification, safety, disposal) and utility angle appeal.
candidates.discover_score_reason: Moderate AI-citation potential — specific and traceable to FDA once notice confirmed, but time-bound/ephemeral.
candidates.notes: Evidence requirements: Moderate — needs FDA primary source before publish; no expert commentary required for straightforward recall explainer.

candidates.allowed_category: wellness trends and skeptical health evaluation
candidates.recommended_angle: NYT already raised skepticism generally — differentiate by going category-by-category (magnesium, B12, 'weight-loss' patches) with independent expert on transdermal absorption science rather than restating NYT's summary.
candidates.why_now: Tier-1 source raising skepticism question; clear SERP gap for independent expert evaluation; no prior coverage in recent content.
candidates.primary_headline: Do Supplement Patches Actually Work? We Asked a Pharmacologist
candidates.next_steps: Commission feature with clinical pharmacologist or dermatologist expert on transdermal delivery; differentiate from NYT angle with category-specific analysis.
integrity_flags: Most patch marketing claims lack peer-reviewed efficacy data — frame as 'no evidence supports' rather than 'proven ineffective' unless a specific study says otherwise.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Moderate trend strength from single tier-1 outlet; sustained consumer interest in wellness patch category.
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: Strong evaluative angle, expert-dependent differentiation, and high consumer search intent for patch efficacy.
candidates.discover_score_reason: Strong AI-citation potential due to clear expert sourcing and category-by-category structure on high-volume search terms.
candidates.notes: Estimated word count 900-1200 words; format is evaluative feature; medium SERP difficulty on primary keyword.
